correctness.rationale: For X=uv^T and Y=st^T write a=v^Ts, b=t^Tu, d=t^Ts and e=v^Tu. The products vanish together for a=b=0 (A choices of Y per X); the only other cancellation is a nonzero multiple of an X of nonzero trace. Two nonzero summands give rank two exactly when both image and row pairs are independent. The restriction to the image span(u,s) has trace zero and determinant −ab(ab−ed). At Delta=0 it is nonzero since ab≠0, so C² has rank one and C³=0, forcing exactly J_3; rank one has square zero by the trace identity. At Delta≠0 the image and kernel split. For the exact count at e=0 take X=E_12 and normalize s_2=1; t_1=ab is nonzero with 2n−2 free coordinates, and Delta=(ab)². In characteristic two the restriction is scalar precisely when d=0; that condition fixes t_2 uniquely given the other coordinates and leaves q^(2n−3) matrices. For e≠0 take X=eE_11 and normalize s_1=1; t_1 is nonzero and s',t' in the remaining coordinates are nonzero. Delta=−e²t_1(t'·s'), with q^(n−2) possible t' for a nonzero dot product and q^(n−2)−1 for zero for each s'. The off-diagonal entry −be forbids a scalar restriction in characteristic two. These counts and the trace-stratum sizes give all rank and spectral formulas, including the vanishing rank-two nilpotent count at n=2.

originality.rationale: There are substantial exact subfamily overlaps. The earlier primitive-idempotent table covers both-nonzero-trace pairs after scaling and mixing over traces. The distinct same-date nilpotent record covers both-trace-zero pairs for n≥3; its specialization supplies the characteristic-two scalar contribution in that range once one proves that a scalar restriction forces both traces to vanish. Neither covers mixed-trace pairs, and the full aggregated rank/Delta/Jordan law is not implied by the two same-stratum censuses. Pass the all-input law, not priority for either subfamily or the standalone nilpotent scalar count.

value.rationale: This gives exact random-pair benchmarks for all rank-one inputs, not only whether a given spectrum is possible. In particular the mixed stratum completes the finite-field law and the repeated-root characteristic-two split reveals types that either homogeneous stratum can miss. The result distinguishes nilpotency of index three, split versus nonsplit factors and scalar versus Jordan restrictions uniformly in dimension and field.
residual_risks: No count of simultaneous-conjugacy classes of input pairs or generalization to higher input ranks is established.
